promotion_note: Promoted 2026-07-30 (owner instruction, pjm-140 session). EXACTLY ONE config delta vs the superseded 2026-07-29-pjm-137-ctheatrate: ramp_limits False -> True. The pjm-137 recipe is otherwise carried VERBATIM (its measured_ct_heat_rates delta, pjm-136's zonal loss surface, pjm-135's net-position cut and pjm-133's hydro budget all preserved), and the A/B control arm pjm140_control_A reproduces the superseded keeper BYTE-IDENTICALLY -- 0.000000000 MW over 166,440 class-hours in each of 2023/2024/2025 -- so the delta is provably isolated. MECHANISM (zero DOF): one two-sided LP row per (plant, CC/CT/ST family) group per hour transition t=1..T-1 bounding that group's summed P move by its MEASURED maximum observed 1-h CAMPD gross-load move, rebased gross->net per plant, widened at availability edges by exactly the capacity discontinuity the model itself imposes. From the existing frozen derive (rule 23) run for PJM for the FIRST time (scripts/data/derive_campd_ramp_envelopes.py --iso PJM -> campd_ramp_envelopes_PJM.csv, 209 rows, 145 well-observed plant-family groups). No scale, no haircut, no blend, no per-plant override, no quantile swap -- PREREG section 5's no-feedback ceiling forbids all of them and the only knob touched was the flag's on/off state. The DOF ledger goes 17 -> 18 entries with n_residual UNCHANGED at 6. Rule 19: no other keeper mechanism owns intertemporal thermal coupling (commitment_enabled and pjm_commitment_posture False, committed_ramp_spread 0.0, the three P1-native bridges ISO-exclusive to CAISO/ERCOT/NYISO, measured_ramp_capability governing reserve ELIGIBILITY not energy ramping). Rule 25: PJM's artifact from PJM's own plants -- ERCOT's R and CAISO's I on this matrix row were reached on different defects and do NOT transfer. DRIVER (rule 14 [R-ACCURATE], not a residual): with ramp_limits off the LP asserts that every thermal plant can move from any output to any other output in one hour. That is false as physics, and the model ACTS on it -- measured on the superseded keeper's own per-unit dispatch, it crosses the measured envelope in 0.393/0.463/0.319 % of 1,699,246 group-transitions (149/167/147 of 194 groups ever cross), carrying 555,882/587,079/536,940 MWh a year of hourly ramping the real PJM fleet's own measured maxima say those machines could not deliver that fast. Arming the envelope cuts that to 51,161/64,048/82,425 MWh -- a 90.8/89.1/84.6 % REDUCTION, i.e. roughly 0.5 TWh/yr of physically infeasible dispatch removed. The residual is BY DESIGN: the availability-edge widening is the row's only slack, so every remaining crossing sits at a capacity discontinuity. COVERAGE (K7 PASS): the loader puts a live envelope on 194 of 323 (plant, family) groups = 124.1 GW = 90.1 % of ramp-eligible thermal capacity (56.7 % of all capacity), pruning only 6 groups (664 MW, 2 CC + 4 CT) as non-binding and leaving 123 CT groups (12.9 GW) with no row at all -- CT gets no class fallback because bang-bang is the measured norm (rule 18 [R-PHYSICS]: no class-name gate anywhere). Live up-envelope median 0.40 of group pmax (p25 0.32 / p75 0.53), down-envelope median 0.53. Gross->net rebasis on 142 measured per-plant EIA-923-net/CAMPD-gross factors (min 0.8252, median 0.9700, max 0.9968) plus 2 cited class defaults (0.9750). GATES (PREREG-pjm140-ramp-envelopes-2026-07-30.md, committed and pushed BEFORE either arm solved): determination CALIBRATED in BOTH arms with EVERY criterion passing -- C1 16/16 with free 12/12, C2/C3a/C3b/C3c/C4/C6/C7/C8 all PASS. K3 the C3c standing kill: C3c PASSES and is IDENTICAL -- model tail-hour counts 3/10/32 h in BOTH arms -- so the keeper's thinnest margin was not touched in either direction. K4 ZERO slack and ZERO dump, both arms, all years, so the envelope is not infeasibly tight. K5 the control arm byte-identical. K7 PASS at 90.1 %. C8 CT_PEAKER forced share UNCHANGED at 16.3/16.9/17.1 %, all GROUNDED (D-4 clear, profile r 0.923-0.973, off-peak CV ratio 0.705-1.084) -- as pre-registered, a ramp row is not a min-gen floor and adds no D-2 mechanism id. D-1/D-2 read FAIL in both arms AND in the superseded keeper's own committed legitimacy_report.md: pre-existing states the rule-20 materiality filter and C7/C8 grounding resolve to PASS, unchanged by the delta. THE PRE-REGISTRATION WAS REFUTED ON MAGNITUDE and is recorded as such rather than re-written (the pjm-137 precedent). K6 the primary -- the DJF h04->h07 model system-price rise -- moves UP in all three years (+3.933->+4.004, +4.554->+4.600, +6.512->+6.546) so K6 passes on direction, but that is +$0.07/+$0.05/+$0.03 against PJM's own measured +15.28/+21.63/+35.45, i.e. only 0.6/0.2/0.1 % of the remaining gap, against a pre-registered claimable ceiling of +$5.55/+$13.44 load-weighted for 2024-25. PREREG section 4 secondary 1 is ALSO refuted: CC_REGULAR moves UP and CT_PEAKER DOWN, the opposite of the predicted direction. WHY: the pjm-139 W7 pre-check compared the model's p99 1-h move against the real fleet's p99 (1.4-1.7x) and inferred that per-plant rows would bind, but the derive writes each plant's MAX pooled over 26,280 hours -- and the model's own p99 sits at 0.281/0.293/0.289 of that max (its MAX at 1.415/1.478/1.361). A MAX-based envelope cannot be pre-checked with a p99-based excess statistic; binding lives in the top fraction of a percent of transitions, so reshaping 0.4 % of transitions buys $0.03-0.07. This is the ERCOT-127 property ('the real fleet violates the envelope 0-10 times a year') now measured on PJM's own fleet. HONEST SCOPE, leading rather than trailing: (a) THE DELTA DOES NOT CLOSE THE WINTER MORNING RAMP and its root cause remains UNIDENTIFIED -- the reachable residual is unchanged at DJF h06-h07 load-weighted -$0.37/+$5.55/+$13.44 after the two closed lanes. (b) The mechanism is NEAR-INERT on dispatch: worst class +0.262/-0.184/-0.219 % of its own energy (COAL_PRB / VIRTUAL_INC / ST_GAS), every MATERIAL class under 0.06 % (CC_REGULAR +0.053/+0.032/+0.009, COAL_BIT -0.019/+0.012, CT_PEAKER -0.158/-0.055), ISO total moving 2-5 GWh out of ~820 TWh. The PREREG's literal K1 inert test (every class < 0.1 %) is NOT met so K1 does not fire, but 'near-inert' is the honest description. (c) OPERATIONAL COST: the rows add 1,699,246 LP rows (each two-sided) and ~23.3 M nonzeros, raising peak RSS from 15.18 to 15.55 GB, so SWAP IS NOW A REQUIREMENT rather than a cushion for a PJM per-plant solve on a 15 GB box -- a successor re-solving this keeper must re-assert swapon /swapfile before every arm. (d) Every limitation inherited from pjm-137/136 stands: C3c passes by only ~1 h (2024) and ~2.5 h (2025) against a 0.5x floor, Dominion CC_REGULAR 2025 overshoots, and the delta does not address the congestion half of the Dominion price deficit. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] order of reasoning, for the record: the delta was chartered and is promoted because the measured envelope is more accurate than the implicit infinite-ramp estimate it replaces -- demonstrably so, at half a TWh a year of infeasible dispatch -- and NOT because it improved the fit, which it essentially did not. A real physical constraint stays in even when the residual does not move; the rubric movement is a consequence, never the justification. Full write-up: results/calibration/FINDING-pjm140-ramp-envelopes-remove-infeasible-ramping-but-not-the-price-shape-2026-07-30.md. Supersedes 2026-07-29-pjm-137-ctheatrate.
note: Open ROOT CAUSES. (1) THE ZONAL-CONGESTION ROUTE TO THE DOMINION CT LEG IS CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT (pjm-137). PJM's own binding-constraint record puts 3.1-6.3 % of its DA congestion rent on zonal-scale interfaces and 0.04-0.24 % on AEP-DOM; the constraints that dominate the DOM-separation hours are Loudoun-County 500/230 kV facilities with BOTH ends inside PJM_Dominion; and intra-Dominion EHV dispersion ($6.18/$8.68/$16.78) EXCEEDS the inter-zonal DOM-AEP spread ($4.76/$6.13/$14.42). Do NOT propose another zonal congestion mechanism for this defect. (2) THE DEFECT HAS BEEN OVERSTATED ~1.9x IN THIS NOTE'S OWN PREDECESSORS: the Dominion CT_PEAKER actual is 3.066/4.048/5.218 TWh on the benchmark's own unit-split per-plant record, NOT the 7.38/8.68/9.64 every prior handoff carried -- that figure is the nine roster plants' WHOLE-PLANT energy and counts Doswell's combined-cycle blocks (4.45 TWh in 2025) as peaker output. The real gap after pjm-137 is -2.345/-2.600/-2.056 TWh, i.e. the model is at 24/36/61 % of actual. Always take a zonal class actual from frontend/data/backcast/bench/<ISO>/<year>.json.gz, which carries split: 'unit_hourly' at mixed sites. (3) THE SUCCESSOR'S TARGET, RESTATED ON THE CORRECTED HOUR KEY (pjm-138 A1 + pjm-139). The Dominion CT-hour price deficit is $17.97/$26.44/$54.06 per MWh, NOT the $17.72/$26.69/$54.61 this note carried: pjm-137's measured-side loader indexed Eastern PREVAILING time against a model and a CAMPD record that are BOTH Eastern STANDARD, so from March to November its series sat one hour ahead of both. Levels move only $0.12-0.38/MWh and every pjm-137 conclusion stands (the correlation improves 0.704->0.745, 0.732->0.764, 0.772->0.823), but NO diurnal statistic may be quoted from _pjm137_dominion_ct_congestion.py -- use _pjm138_mec_gap_shape.py's UTC-keyed loader. OF THAT DEFICIT, ONLY 8.1/23.1/22.1 % IS REACHABLE: pjm-137 closed 54.6/51.8/54.2 % as intra-zonal congestion and pjm-138 attributes 37.3/25.2/26.2 % to the reserve opportunity cost the no-MIP LP structurally cannot price, leaving $1.46/$6.12/$11.97 per MWh for ANY energy-stack mechanism. Crediting the measured reserve price takes the ANNUAL load-weighted system-energy gap to -$2.36/-$0.08/+$2.76 -- the energy stack's LEVEL is right and the residual is SHAPE ONLY, so any lever must raise tight hours WITHOUT raising slack ones. AND THE REACHABLE SHARE IS CONCENTRATED, NOT SPREAD ACROSS CT HOURS (pjm-139): it lives in the WINTER MORNING RAMP. DJF h06-h07 CT-weighted the residual after both closed lanes is $3.93/$30.48/$40.11 (load-weighted after the reserve credit -$0.37/+$5.55/+$13.44, so 2023 is fully explained and 2024-25 are not), while DJF midday and overnight run NEGATIVE -- the model is too DEAR there. The defect is a RAMP-RATE deficit, not a level or a fuel-price one: PJM's own DJF system energy price rises +$15.28/+$21.63/+$35.45 from h04 to h07 and the model's rises +$3.93/+$4.55/+$6.51, 26/21/18 % of it, and the model's whole-day DJF trough-to-peak range is 32/27/21 % of PJM's. Root cause measured: the keeper runs ramp_limits=False, so the LP has NO intertemporal thermal coupling and meets the winter morning ramp with STEAM it ramps 1.8/2.4/2.6x harder than the real fleet instead of the CTs PJM actually starts (model CT rise only 58/76/83 % of actual) -- which also predicts the standing CT_PEAKER -2.11/-3.57/-3.32 TWh C1 note. THE CHARTERED SUCCESSOR LEVER IS NOW SPENT AND THE DEFECT IS STILL OPEN (pjm-140). ramp_envelopes was armed, A/B tested across all three years and PROMOTED -- it is matrix PJM K and lives in this keeper -- but it moves the DJF h04->h07 rise only +$0.07/+$0.05/+$0.03 (0.6/0.2/0.1 % of the remaining gap), so the winter morning ramp's ROOT CAUSE REMAINS UNIDENTIFIED. It was promoted on rule 1/rule 14 physics grounds, not on fit: it removes 85-91 % of the keeper's physically infeasible hourly ramping (~0.5 TWh/yr). The pjm-139 W7 pre-check misfired because it compared the model's p99 1-h move to the real fleet's p99 (1.4-1.7x) while the envelope is each plant's MAX, and the model's own p99 is only 0.28x that max -- DO NOT pre-check a MAX-based bound with a p99-based excess statistic, in any ISO. PREREG section 5 forbids tuning the envelope (no quantile swap, no tightening, no scaling), so there is no second version of this lever: a binding ramp representation needs a DIFFERENT mechanism with its own charter. See FINDING-pjm140-ramp-envelopes-remove-infeasible-ramping-but-not-the-price-shape-2026-07-30.md and FINDING-pjm139-winter-morning-ramp-is-a-ramp-rate-deficit-2026-07-30.md. Refused until a measured sub-zonal load basis exists. (5) C8 CT_PEAKER forced share rose to 16.3/16.9/17.1 % at pjm-137 (all GROUNDED) on a class whose volume fell 2.6-2.9 TWh -- watch it. The intervening keeper line (the CC_LIKE mid-curve belt, the pjm-135 net-position cut, the pjm-136 zonal loss surface, the pjm-137 measured CT heat rates) is the plausible cause. DO NOT re-run pjm-122's charge as a live diagnosis. (b) THE RESERVE / LP SUPPLY-SIDE TIGHTNESS LANE IS NOT A MISSING MECHANISM. PJM's own published day-ahead market prices synchronized reserve above zero in 84.2/96.7/47.6 % of ALL hours at a cover ratio of 1.00-1.11 and the model's reserve dual is above zero in 0/2/28 hours of 8,760 -- but the requirement is PJM's own measured series (load_pjm_measured_reserve_requirement, validated to 2-4 % against PJM's published DA requirement), the demand curve is PJM's published two-step ORDC (pjm_ordc_curve.csv, M11 4.3.3, $850/$300) and the in-LP per-generator joint-headroom co-optimization that is DESIGNED to price the opportunity cost is armed and is its SOLE owner under rule 19. Lane owner-closed 2026-07-11; requirement-side dynamic reserves adjudicated INERT by measurement. Do NOT propose a reserve/scarcity mechanism for PJM.
